title: Can exact edit distance be computed in truly subquadratic time?
formal: Is there an ε>0 and a deterministic algorithm computing exact unit-cost edit distance between two length-n strings over a fixed finite alphabet in O(n^(2−ε)) time?
context:
Fix the standard word-RAM model with O(log n)-bit words. Approximation algorithms and logarithmic improvements to quadratic time do not meet the target; a classical deterministic algorithm of this form would refute SETH.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: A fundamental quadratic barrier for string comparison and a principal example in fine-grained complexity.
